An **agent trace** is a record of how an AI agent handled a task: the sequence of steps involved, such as model calls, tool use, handoffs, and results. The term varies by platform. **Example:** A user asks for the weather; the agent calls a weather tool, receives its result, and replies. A trace might show the model call, the tool call and its input and output, and the final response, along with timing or errors.

Traces help people inspect, debug, and evaluate an agent’s behavior. Depending on configuration, it may contain sensitive inputs or outputs, so traces should be handled accordingly.

**Sources:** [OpenAI Agents SDK — Tracing](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tracing/); [OpenTelemetry — Traces](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/traces/); [LangSmith — Tracing](https://docs.smith.langchain.com/observability/concepts#traces).

Depending on configuration, it may contain sensitive inputs or outputs, so traces should be handled accordingly.
